    13→<decisions>
    14→## Implementation Decisions
    15→
    16→### TOTP Enrollment (fc-1)
    17→- 2FA is optional, user-enabled via Settings page (single-user app, no mandatory enforcement needed)
    18→- Enrollment flow: QR code + manual secret display in Settings, compatible with Google Authenticator/Authy/1Password
    19→- Generate 8 one-time recovery codes at enrollment time (essential safety net if authenticator device is lost)

1→# Phase 9: Feature Expansion - Research
     2→
     3→**Researched:** 2026-03-19
     4→**Domain:** TOTP/2FA authentication + server-side SQLite backup automation
     5→**Confidence:** HIGH
     6→
     7→## Summary
     8→
     9→Phase 9 implements two independent server-side features: optional TOTP-based 2FA for password login, and automated daily backup of the /data directory. Both features integrate with established Phase 7 infrastructure (audit logging, alerter, metrics) and the existing node-cron scheduler pattern in scheduler.ts.
    10→
    11→The TOTP feature requires one new npm dependency (`otpauth` 9.5.0) and a QR code renderer on the desktop client (the `qrcode` library is the standard choice, version 1.5.4). The backup feature requires no new dependencies — better-sqlite3 (already present at ^12.6.2) provides the `.backup()` API, and Node.js built-in `node:fs`, `node:path`, and `node:zlib` handle archive creation without needing `node-tar`. The `fs.createReadStream`/`zlib.createGzip`/`fs.createWriteStream` pipeline is idiomatic Node.js for tar.gz creation.
    12→
    13→The TOTP enrollment and verification flow intercepts the existing `loginWithPassword()` path in `password.ts`. After a successful password check, the server returns an intermediate state (`{ needsTotp: true, totpToken: <short-lived-nonce> }`) instead of a session token. The client presents a TOTP challenge screen, submits the code to a new `/totp/verify` endpoint, and receives the real session token on success. All TOTP metadata is stored in a new `totp` table keyed to the user, separate from the `auth` table which stores the password hash.
    14→
    15→**Primary recommendation:** Implement TOTP using `otpauth` for secret generation and verification. Use `qrcode` for QR rendering on the client. Extend `scheduler.ts` with a second `cron.schedule()` call for backup. Store TOTP secrets AES-256-GCM encrypted using a server-derived key (PBKDF2 from server secret). Archive backups with Node.js built-in streams.

   114→## Architecture Patterns
   115→
   116→### Recommended File Structure
   117→
   118→```
   119→packages/sync-server/src/
   120→├── accounts/
   121→│   ├── password.ts               # EXISTING — add TOTP check after password success
   122→│   └── totp.ts                   # NEW — enrollTotp(), verifyTotpCode(), disableTotp(),
   123→│                                 #        verifyRecoveryCode(), generateRecoveryCodes()
   124→├── util/
   125→│   ├── audit.ts                  # EXISTING — add totp_* event types to AuditEventType
   126→│   ├── audit-migrations.ts       # EXISTING — add totp table migration here (idempotent)
   127→│   └── backup.ts                 # NEW — runBackup(), cleanOldBackups(), getBackupStatus()
   128→├── app-account.ts                # EXISTING — add /totp/setup, /totp/verify-setup,
   129→│                                 #            /totp/challenge, /totp/disable, /totp/status
   130→└── scheduler.ts                  # EXISTING — add second cron.schedule() for backup
   131→
   132→packages/desktop-client/src/components/settings/
   133→├── TwoFactorSettings.tsx         # NEW — enroll/disable TOTP, show QR, copy recovery codes
   134→└── BackupStatus.tsx              # NEW — last backup time, status, optional "Backup Now" button
   135→```
   136→
   137→### Pattern 1: Intermediate TOTP Challenge State
   138→
   139→The login endpoint cannot return a session token when TOTP is enrolled; it must return a short-lived nonce the client uses to complete the TOTP challenge.
   140→
   141→**What:** After `loginWithPassword()` succeeds, check if TOTP is enrolled. If yes, generate a short-lived nonce (UUID, expires in 5 minutes, stored in-memory Map), return `{ needsTotp: true, totpNonce: <nonce> }` instead of `{ token }`. Client calls `/totp/challenge` with `{ totpNonce, code }` to redeem the nonce for a real session token.
   142→
   143→**When to use:** Only on the `default` (password) branch of the `/login` switch in `app-account.ts`. OpenID and header branches are unaffected.
   144→
   145→**Example (server-side login modification):**
   146→```typescript
   147→// In app-account.ts /login — after tokenRes = loginWithPassword(password)
   148→if (!tokenRes.error && isTotpEnrolled()) {
   149→  const nonce = uuidv4();
   150→  totpNonces.set(nonce, { expiresAt: Date.now() + 5 * 60 * 1000 });
   151→  res.send({ status: 'ok', data: { needsTotp: true, totpNonce: nonce } });
   152→  return;
   153→}
   154→```
   155→
   156→### Pattern 2: TOTP Secret Storage (Encrypted)
   157→
   158→**What:** Store TOTP secret AES-256-GCM encrypted. Key derived from `process.env.SECRET_KEY` (already used in Phase 5.2) + a fixed salt using PBKDF2 (100K iterations, same as existing password key derivation pattern). Store `{ iv, authTag, ciphertext }` as JSON in a new `totp` table.
   159→
   160→**Schema (added to `runAuditMigrations()` pattern — new idempotent migration helper):**
   161→```sql
   162→CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS totp (
   163→  id           INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
   164→  user_id      TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
   165→  secret_enc   TEXT    NOT NULL,  -- JSON: { iv, authTag, ciphertext } base64-encoded
   166→  enrolled_at  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%s','now')),
   167→  last_used_at INTEGER,           -- epoch seconds, for replay prevention
   168→  recovery_codes TEXT NOT NULL    -- JSON array of bcrypt hashes
   169→);
   170→```
   171→
   172→Note: CONTEXT.md says "Store TOTP secret encrypted in `auth` table with method='totp'". However, the `auth` table's `extra_data` column stores only a single text blob (currently the bcrypt password hash). Storing a structured JSON blob in `extra_data` would work functionally but mixes concerns. The clean approach — and what the planner should verify — is a separate `totp` table. Both approaches are viable; the planner should pick one consistently. **Recommendation: separate `totp` table for clarity and replay-prevention (`last_used_at` column).**
   173→
   174→### Pattern 3: Backup Cron Extension
   175→
   176→**What:** Add a second `cron.schedule()` call in `startScheduler()`, guarded by `ENABLE_AUTO_BACKUP !== 'false'` (opt-out, enabled by default — matches the decision that backup is a safety feature).
   177→
   178→**Example:**
   179→```typescript
   180→// scheduler.ts — inside startScheduler(), after existing sync cron
   181→const backupSchedule = process.env.BACKUP_CRON_SCHEDULE ?? '0 2 * * *';
   182→cron.schedule(backupSchedule, () => {
   183→  runBackup().catch(err => {
   184→    logger.error('Backup failed', { error: err.message });
   185→    triggerAlert({
   186→      event_type: 'backup_failure',
   187→      message: `Daily backup failed: ${err.message}`,
   188→      severity: 'error',
   189→    }).catch(() => {});
   190→  });
   191→});
   192→logger.info('Auto-backup scheduled', { schedule: backupSchedule });
   193→```
   194→
   195→### Pattern 4: SQLite Hot Backup via better-sqlite3
   196→
   197→**What:** `better-sqlite3`'s `.backup(destPath)` API performs an online backup (safe while the DB is open and being written to). It returns a Promise. Used in `exportDatabase()` in `index.electron.ts` — the same pattern applies in sync-server.
   198→
   199→**Source:** Confirmed in `packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.electron.ts` line 128: `await db.backup(name)`.
   200→
   201→The sync-server uses `WrappedDatabase` (db.ts) which wraps `better-sqlite3`. The underlying database is accessible; the backup function must open a raw `better-sqlite3` instance pointed at `account.sqlite`, call `.backup(destPath)`, then close it.
   202→
   203→**Example:**
   204→```typescript
   205→import Database from 'better-sqlite3';
   206→
   207→// Backup account.sqlite atomically
   208→const src = new Database(srcPath, { readonly: true });
   209→await src.backup(destPath);
   210→src.close();
   211→```
   212→
   213→### Pattern 5: Recovery Code Generation and Verification
   214→
   215→**What:** Generate 8 codes of format `XXXX-XXXX-XXXX` (12 alphanumeric chars in 3 groups of 4). Use `crypto.randomBytes(6).toString('hex').toUpperCase()` per code, split into groups. Hash each with bcrypt (cost 10 — lower than password's 12 since recovery codes are long random strings). Store as JSON array in `totp.recovery_codes`.
   216→
   217→On verification: iterate hashes, `bcrypt.compareSync(submitted, hash)`. On match, remove that hash from the array and save (mark consumed). Return `{ valid: true, remaining: N }`.
   218→
   219→### Anti-Patterns to Avoid
   220→
   221→- **Using `auth` table `extra_data` for structured TOTP data**: The column is a single text blob currently used for the bcrypt password hash. Overloading it requires JSON parsing everywhere and makes `extra_data` semantics ambiguous.
   222→- **Calling `loginWithPassword()` to check enrollment**: TOTP enrollment check must happen outside `loginWithPassword()` (which returns a token) — check after the call returns success.
   223→- **Synchronous file operations for backup**: Backup involves large file copies; use async Node.js fs promises (`fs.promises.copyFile`, etc.) or the async `db.backup()` to avoid blocking the event loop.
   224→- **Storing TOTP nonces in SQLite**: The intermediate nonces (5-min TTL) are ephemeral — an in-memory Map is correct (no persistence needed, no DB overhead).
   225→- **Using node-tar for archive creation**: Unnecessary dependency. Node.js built-in `tar` via pipe (`fs.createReadStream | zlib.createGzip | fs.createWriteStream`) handles the archive.
   226→- **Not scoping tar.gz to relative paths**: Archive budget directories with relative paths (not absolute) so the archive can be extracted anywhere. Use `path.relative(dataDir, filePath)` as entry name.
   227→
   228→---
   229→
   230→## Don't Hand-Roll
   231→
   232→| Problem | Don't Build | Use Instead | Why |
   233→|---------|-------------|-------------|-----|
   234→| TOTP secret generation + verification | Custom HMAC-based OTP | `otpauth` | RFC 6238 compliance, time-window handling, QR URI generation |
   235→| QR code rendering | SVG/canvas from scratch | `qrcode` library | Correct QR error correction levels, supports both server-side data URI and client-side canvas rendering |
   236→| SQLite hot backup | File copy while DB open | `db.backup(destPath)` from better-sqlite3 | Atomic, WAL-aware, prevents corruption during concurrent writes |
   237→| TOTP QR URI format | Custom URI string | `otpauth.TOTP.toString()` | Generates correct `otpauth://` URI that authenticator apps parse |
   238→
   239→**Key insight:** The TOTP protocol has subtle edge cases (time window, replay prevention, base32 encoding) that `otpauth` handles correctly. The backup API has OS-level file locking concerns that `better-sqlite3`'s `.backup()` resolves. Do not implement either from scratch.
   240→
   241→---
   242→
   243→## Common Pitfalls
   244→
   245→### Pitfall 1: TOTP Replay Attack Within Tolerance Window
   246→**What goes wrong:** The 1-step tolerance window allows codes valid 30 seconds before/after the current period. If the same code is accepted twice within this window, an attacker who intercepts the code can reuse it.
   247→**Why it happens:** Naive implementations only check if the code is valid, not if it was already used.
   248→**How to avoid:** Store `last_used_at` as the epoch timestamp of the TOTP period (floor to 30s boundary) in the `totp` table. Reject any code whose period timestamp equals `last_used_at`. Update `last_used_at` on successful verification.
   249→**Warning signs:** No `last_used_at` column in the TOTP schema.
   250→
   251→### Pitfall 2: Intermediate Nonce Leaking Password Correctness
   252→**What goes wrong:** If the server returns `{ needsTotp: true }` only after a valid password, an attacker can use the response to enumerate whether the password was correct.
   253→**Why it happens:** The two-step flow inherently leaks this.
   254→**How to avoid:** This is a known, accepted tradeoff for single-user apps (CONTEXT.md decision). For the implementation, ensure that failed TOTP attempts after a correct password still hit `trackAuthFailure()` and `writeAuditLog()` so the burst alerter fires on TOTP brute-force.
   255→**Warning signs:** TOTP failures not calling `trackAuthFailure(req.ip)`.
   256→
   257→### Pitfall 3: `auth` Table Method Collision
   258→**What goes wrong:** CONTEXT.md says store TOTP secret in `auth` table with `method='totp'`. The `auth` table currently has `extra_data TEXT` which stores a bcrypt hash for `method='password'`. Inserting a TOTP row with a JSON blob in `extra_data` works but the `needsBootstrap()` function checks `rows.length === 0` — a TOTP row would make the app think it's bootstrapped even with no password.
   259→**Why it happens:** `needsBootstrap()` does `SELECT * FROM auth` and returns `rows.length === 0`. Adding a `method='totp'` row would always return false.
   260→**How to avoid:** Use a separate `totp` table (not `auth` table). If the planner decides to follow the CONTEXT.md suggestion of `auth` table, `needsBootstrap()` must be updated to check `WHERE method = 'password' OR method = 'openid'`.
   261→**Warning signs:** `needsBootstrap()` returning false on a fresh install after TOTP migration runs.
   262→
   263→### Pitfall 4: Backup Running While SQLite is Being Written
   264→**What goes wrong:** If backup starts at 2 AM during an active sync (unlikely but possible), a naive file copy produces a corrupt backup.
   265→**Why it happens:** SQLite WAL mode allows concurrent readers but a raw `cp` skips WAL coordination.
   266→**How to avoid:** Always use `db.backup(destPath)` from better-sqlite3, which coordinates with the WAL and produces a consistent snapshot. Never use `fs.copyFile` directly on a live SQLite database.
   267→**Warning signs:** Using `fs.promises.copyFile` on `.sqlite` files instead of `db.backup()`.
   268→
   269→### Pitfall 5: Budget File Discovery
   270→**What goes wrong:** The backup needs to find all budget SQLite files under `/data`. The directory structure is `{ACTUAL_DATA_DIR}/{budget-uuid}/db.sqlite`. A hardcoded path will miss budgets or include unexpected files.
   271→**Why it happens:** Budget directories are UUID-named subdirectories; there's no registry of them outside the filesystem.
   272→**How to avoid:** Scan `ACTUAL_DATA_DIR` for subdirectories containing `db.sqlite`. Exclude the `backups/` directory itself from scanning to avoid recursive backup attempts.
   273→**Warning signs:** Hardcoded paths, not scanning for `db.sqlite` dynamically.
   274→
   275→### Pitfall 6: Recovery Codes Shown Once
   276→**What goes wrong:** If recovery codes are regenerated or re-shown after enrollment, users may assume the old codes are still valid.
   277→**Why it happens:** Poor state management of the enrollment flow.
   278→**How to avoid:** The server never returns plaintext recovery codes after the initial enrollment response. The `/totp/setup` endpoint returns codes once; subsequent `/totp/status` calls return only `{ enrolled: true, recoveryCodesRemaining: N }`. The client must make this clear with "Download / Copy now — these will not be shown again" UI.
   279→**Warning signs:** `/totp/status` returning plaintext codes.
   280→
   281→---
   282→
   283→## Code Examples
   284→
   285→### TOTP Secret Generation and QR URI (otpauth 9.5.0)
   286→
   287→```typescript
   288→// Source: otpauth npm package docs (verified 2026-03-19)
   289→import { TOTP } from 'otpauth';
   290→
   291→// Generate a new TOTP secret for enrollment
   292→export function generateTotpSecret(issuer: string, accountName: string) {
   293→  const totp = new TOTP({
   294→    issuer,
   295→    label: accountName,
   296→    algorithm: 'SHA1',
   297→    digits: 6,
   298→    period: 30,
   299→  });
   300→  // totp.secret is the base32-encoded secret
   301→  // totp.toString() produces the otpauth:// URI for QR codes
   302→  return {
   303→    secret: totp.secret.base32,
   304→    uri: totp.toString(),
   305→  };
   306→}
   307→
   308→// Verify a TOTP code with 1-step window tolerance
   309→export function verifyTotpCode(
   310→  secret: string,
   311→  code: string,
   312→  lastUsedAt: number | null,
   313→): { valid: boolean; usedAt: number } {
   314→  const totp = new TOTP({ secret, algorithm: 'SHA1', digits: 6, period: 30 });
   315→  const delta = totp.validate({ token: code, window: 1 });
   316→  if (delta === null) return { valid: false, usedAt: lastUsedAt ?? 0 };
   317→
   318→  // The period timestamp for replay prevention
   319→  const periodTs = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000 / 30) + delta;
   320→  if (lastUsedAt !== null && periodTs === lastUsedAt) {
   321→    return { valid: false, usedAt: lastUsedAt }; // replay
   322→  }
   323→  return { valid: true, usedAt: periodTs };
   324→}
   325→```
   326→
   327→### QR Code Rendering (qrcode 1.5.4, server-side data URI)
   328→
   329→```typescript
   330→// Source: qrcode npm package (verified 2026-03-19)
   331→import QRCode from 'qrcode';
   332→
   333→// Called in /totp/setup endpoint — returns data URI for the client to render as <img>
   334→export async function generateQrDataUri(otpauthUri: string): Promise<string> {
   335→  return QRCode.toDataURL(otpauthUri, { errorCorrectionLevel: 'M' });
   336→}
   337→```
   338→
   339→### Backup Cron Registration in scheduler.ts
   340→
   341→```typescript
   342→// Extends existing startScheduler() — second cron.schedule() call
   343→const backupSchedule = process.env.BACKUP_CRON_SCHEDULE ?? '0 2 * * *';
   344→if (process.env.ENABLE_AUTO_BACKUP !== 'false') {
   345→  cron.schedule(backupSchedule, () => {
   346→    runBackup().catch(err => {
   347→      logger.error('Backup cron failed', { error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) });
   348→      triggerAlert({
   349→        event_type: 'backup_failure',
   350→        message: `Daily backup failed: ${err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)}`,
   351→        severity: 'error',
   352→      }).catch(() => {});
   353→    });
   354→  });
   355→  logger.info('Auto-backup scheduled', { schedule: backupSchedule });
   356→}
   357→```
   358→
   359→### SQLite Hot Backup via better-sqlite3
   360→
   361→```typescript
   362→// Source: better-sqlite3 docs + confirmed usage in index.electron.ts line 128
   363→import Database from 'better-sqlite3';
   364→import { promises as fsp } from 'node:fs';
   365→import path from 'node:path';
   366→
   367→export async function backupSqliteFile(srcPath: string, destPath: string): Promise<void> {
   368→  await fsp.mkdir(path.dirname(destPath), { recursive: true });
   369→  const db = new Database(srcPath, { readonly: true });
   370→  try {
   371→    await db.backup(destPath);
   372→  } finally {
   373→    db.close();
   374→  }
   375→}
   376→```

**Project:** Actual Budget Fork - Enable Banking Edition
**Core Value:** Automatic bank transaction sync that works for EU accounts without manual data entry
**Depth:** Comprehensive
**Created:** 2026-02-18

## Phases

- [-] **Phase 1: Foundation and API Client** - Fork is running, Enable Banking API client is sandbox-tested with RSA auth

## Phase Details

### Phase 1: Foundation and API Client

**Goal:** The forked Actual Budget repo builds and runs in Docker, RSA key auth with Enable Banking is verified against the sandbox, and fork hygiene discipline is established before any custom code is written.

**Depends on:** Nothing (first phase)

**Requirements:** FOUND-01, FOUND-02, FOUND-03, FOUND-04

**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE when this phase completes):

1. Running `docker compose up` starts the sync-server and desktop-client with no build errors, and the user can open the app in Chrome and create a budget
2. An Enable Banking sandbox API call authenticated with the RSA key pair returns a 200 response (not a 401 or JWT error)
3. The RSA private key file survives a `docker compose down && docker compose up` cycle without being regenerated
4. Every custom commit in the repo carries an `[eb]` prefix tag distinguishing it from upstream commits

**Research flag:** Read `packages/sync-server/src/app-gocardless/` before implementing `app-enablebanking/` to confirm the current adapter interface (GoCardless may have been refactored since July 2025).

**Plans:** 4 plans

- [x] 01-04-PLAN.md - Gap closure: fix missing [eb] tag on commit 371f06e2e (FOUND-04)

### Phase 2: Bank Sync Pipeline

**Goal:** A user can connect a bank account through the Enable Banking OAuth flow, link it to an Actual account, trigger a manual sync, and see imported transactions with correct balances - with full deduplication of pending-to-booked state transitions.

**Depends on:** Phase 1

**Requirements:** SYNC-01, SYNC-02, SYNC-03, SYNC-04, SYNC-05, SYNC-06, SYNC-07, SYNC-08, SYNC-09

**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE when this phase completes):

1. User clicks "Add bank" in the UI, is redirected to their sandbox bank's login page, completes auth, and returns to the app with bank accounts visible and ready to link
2. User maps a bank account to an Actual account and triggers a manual sync that imports transactions into the correct account ledger
3. Running two syncs in a row does not create duplicate transactions (deduplication works across pending-to-booked transitions)
4. Account balances shown in Actual match the balances returned by the Enable Banking API after each sync
5. Each transaction in the ledger shows a visual indicator distinguishing pending (PDNG) from booked (BOOK) status
6. User can connect a second bank under a separate Enable Banking session without breaking the first connection
7. The account view shows last sync time and the most recent sync error (if any) for each linked account
8. Sync events are appended to a log file or DB table that can be inspected for debugging
9. Imported transactions from common EU merchants (grocery chains, utilities, subscriptions, transport) are automatically assigned categories via pre-populated rules

**Research flag:** Standard patterns. `processBankSyncDownload()` and `reconcileTransactions()` are shared loot-core APIs documented in the GoCardless adapter. No additional research needed.

**Plans:** 4/5 plans executed

**Depends on:** Phase 2

**Requirements:** AUTO-01, AUTO-02, AUTO-03, AUTO-04, AUTO-05, AUTO-06

2. Opening the app after 6+ hours of inactivity triggers an automatic sync within seconds, before the user takes any manual action
3. Each linked account shows a "last synced" timestamp that updates after every sync run (automatic or manual)
4. When a bank session is within 14 days of its consent expiry date, a banner appears in the app prompting re-authorization
5. User clicks the re-authorization banner, completes the OAuth redirect at their bank, and sync resumes without data loss
6. The consent expiry date stored for each bank reflects the `maximum_consent_validity` from the Enable Banking session response - not a hardcoded 90 or 180 day value

   114→3. Each linked account shows a "last synced" timestamp that updates after every sync run (automatic or manual)

    14→## Implementation Decisions
    15→
    16→### TOTP Enrollment (fc-1)
    17→- 2FA is optional, user-enabled via Settings page (single-user app, no mandatory enforcement needed)
    18→- Enrollment flow: QR code + manual secret display in Settings, compatible with Google Authenticator/Authy/1Password
    19→- Generate 8 one-time recovery codes at enrollment time (essential safety net if authenticator device is lost)
    20→- Store TOTP secret encrypted in `auth` table with method='totp', recovery codes hashed in separate table or JSON field
    21→- Use `otpauth` npm library (modern, ESM-native, zero-dependency, well-maintained)
    22→- Audit log enrollment and disable events via existing Phase 7 audit system
    23→
    24→### TOTP Verification (fc-1)
    25→- Two-step login: password verification first, then TOTP challenge on a separate screen (doesn't leak password correctness to unenrolled users)
    26→- TOTP required only for password login, not OpenID (OpenID providers handle their own MFA)
    27→- 1-step time window tolerance (30 seconds before/after current period) to handle clock drift
    28→- Track last used TOTP timestamp to prevent replay attacks within the tolerance window
    29→- Recovery codes accepted as TOTP alternative, each code single-use, mark as consumed after use
    30→- Failed TOTP attempts logged to audit log, count toward existing auth failure burst alert (Phase 7)
    31→
    32→### Backup Automation (fc-2)
    33→- Server-side cron job in scheduler.ts (extends existing node-cron pattern, runs without browser open)
    34→- Daily backup at 2 AM via node-cron (5-field format: `0 2 * * *`)
    35→- Back up full /data directory: account.sqlite + all budget SQLite files
    36→- Use SQLite `.backup()` API for atomic database copy (prevents corruption from concurrent access)
    37→- Archive budget directories into tar.gz for space efficiency
    38→- Store backups in /data/backups/ within Docker volume (persists across restarts, no cloud dependency)
    39→
    40→### Backup Retention (fc-2)
    41→- Keep last 7 daily backups (one week of snapshots, sufficient for personal use)
    42→- Automatic cleanup of backups older than 7 days after each successful backup run
    43→- Backup failure triggers alert via existing Phase 7 webhook alerter (new event_type: 'backup_failure')
    44→- Show last backup time and status on Settings page (matches sync status visibility pattern)

    47→- TOTP QR code rendering approach (inline SVG, canvas, or library like `qrcode`)

    49→- TOTP secret encryption key derivation (reuse existing PBKDF2 infrastructure or separate)

1→# Phase 9: Feature Expansion - Research
     2→
     3→**Researched:** 2026-03-19
     4→**Domain:** TOTP/2FA authentication + server-side SQLite backup automation
     5→**Confidence:** HIGH
     6→
     7→## Summary
     8→
     9→Phase 9 implements two independent server-side features: optional TOTP-based 2FA for password login, and automated daily backup of the /data directory. Both features integrate with established Phase 7 infrastructure (audit logging, alerter, metrics) and the existing node-cron scheduler pattern in scheduler.ts.
    10→
    11→The TOTP feature requires one new npm dependency (`otpauth` 9.5.0) and a QR code renderer on the desktop client (the `qrcode` library is the standard choice, version 1.5.4). The backup feature requires no new dependencies — better-sqlite3 (already present at ^12.6.2) provides the `.backup()` API, and Node.js built-in `node:fs`, `node:path`, and `node:zlib` handle archive creation without needing `node-tar`. The `fs.createReadStream`/`zlib.createGzip`/`fs.createWriteStream` pipeline is idiomatic Node.js for tar.gz creation.
    12→
    13→The TOTP enrollment and verification flow intercepts the existing `loginWithPassword()` path in `password.ts`. After a successful password check, the server returns an intermediate state (`{ needsTotp: true, totpToken: <short-lived-nonce> }`) instead of a session token. The client presents a TOTP challenge screen, submits the code to a new `/totp/verify` endpoint, and receives the real session token on success. All TOTP metadata is stored in a new `totp` table keyed to the user, separate from the `auth` table which stores the password hash.
    14→
    15→**Primary recommendation:** Implement TOTP using `otpauth` for secret generation and verification. Use `qrcode` for QR rendering on the client. Extend `scheduler.ts` with a second `cron.schedule()` call for backup. Store TOTP secrets AES-256-GCM encrypted using a server-derived key (PBKDF2 from server secret). Archive backups with Node.js built-in streams.
    16→

   115→
   116→### Recommended File Structure
   117→
   118→```
   119→packages/sync-server/src/
   120→├── accounts/
   121→│   ├── password.ts               # EXISTING — add TOTP check after password success
   122→│   └── totp.ts                   # NEW — enrollTotp(), verifyTotpCode(), disableTotp(),
   123→│                                 #        verifyRecoveryCode(), generateRecoveryCodes()
   124→├── util/
   125→│   ├── audit.ts                  # EXISTING — add totp_* event types to AuditEventType
   126→│   ├── audit-migrations.ts       # EXISTING — add totp table migration here (idempotent)
   127→│   └── backup.ts                 # NEW — runBackup(), cleanOldBackups(), getBackupStatus()
   128→├── app-account.ts                # EXISTING — add /totp/setup, /totp/verify-setup,
   129→│                                 #            /totp/challenge, /totp/disable, /totp/status
   130→└── scheduler.ts                  # EXISTING — add second cron.schedule() for backup
   131→
   132→packages/desktop-client/src/components/settings/
   133→├── TwoFactorSettings.tsx         # NEW — enroll/disable TOTP, show QR, copy recovery codes

   136→
   137→### Pattern 1: Intermediate TOTP Challenge State
   138→
   139→The login endpoint cannot return a session token when TOTP is enrolled; it must return a short-lived nonce the client uses to complete the TOTP challenge.
   140→
   141→**What:** After `loginWithPassword()` succeeds, check if TOTP is enrolled. If yes, generate a short-lived nonce (UUID, expires in 5 minutes, stored in-memory Map), return `{ needsTotp: true, totpNonce: <nonce> }` instead of `{ token }`. Client calls `/totp/challenge` with `{ totpNonce, code }` to redeem the nonce for a real session token.
   142→
   143→**When to use:** Only on the `default` (password) branch of the `/login` switch in `app-account.ts`. OpenID and header branches are unaffected.
   144→
   145→**Example (server-side login modification):**
   146→```typescript
   147→// In app-account.ts /login — after tokenRes = loginWithPassword(password)
   148→if (!tokenRes.error && isTotpEnrolled()) {
   149→  const nonce = uuidv4();
   150→  totpNonces.set(nonce, { expiresAt: Date.now() + 5 * 60 * 1000 });
   151→  res.send({ status: 'ok', data: { needsTotp: true, totpNonce: nonce } });
   152→  return;
   153→}
   154→```
   155→
   156→### Pattern 2: TOTP Secret Storage (Encrypted)
   157→
   158→**What:** Store TOTP secret AES-256-GCM encrypted. Key derived from `process.env.SECRET_KEY` (already used in Phase 5.2) + a fixed salt using PBKDF2 (100K iterations, same as existing password key derivation pattern). Store `{ iv, authTag, ciphertext }` as JSON in a new `totp` table.
   159→
   160→**Schema (added to `runAuditMigrations()` pattern — new idempotent migration helper):**
   161→```sql
   162→CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS totp (
   163→  id           INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
   164→  user_id      TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
   165→  secret_enc   TEXT    NOT NULL,  -- JSON: { iv, authTag, ciphertext } base64-encoded
   166→  enrolled_at  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%s','now')),
   167→  last_used_at INTEGER,           -- epoch seconds, for replay prevention
   168→  recovery_codes TEXT NOT NULL    -- JSON array of bcrypt hashes
   169→);
   170→```
   171→
   172→Note: CONTEXT.md says "Store TOTP secret encrypted in `auth` table with method='totp'". However, the `auth` table's `extra_data` column stores only a single text blob (currently the bcrypt password hash). Storing a structured JSON blob in `extra_data` would work functionally but mixes concerns. The clean approach — and what the planner should verify — is a separate `totp` table. Both approaches are viable; the planner should pick one consistently. **Recommendation: separate `totp` table for clarity and replay-prevention (`last_used_at` column).**
   173→
   174→### Pattern 3: Backup Cron Extension
   175→
   176→**What:** Add a second `cron.schedule()` call in `startScheduler()`, guarded by `ENABLE_AUTO_BACKUP !== 'false'` (opt-out, enabled by default — matches the decision that backup is a safety feature).
   177→
   178→**Example:**
   179→```typescript
   180→// scheduler.ts — inside startScheduler(), after existing sync cron
   181→const backupSchedule = process.env.BACKUP_CRON_SCHEDULE ?? '0 2 * * *';
   182→cron.schedule(backupSchedule, () => {
   183→  runBackup().catch(err => {
   184→    logger.error('Backup failed', { error: err.message });
   185→    triggerAlert({
   186→      event_type: 'backup_failure',
   187→      message: `Daily backup failed: ${err.message}`,
   188→      severity: 'error',
   189→    }).catch(() => {});
   190→  });
   191→});
   192→logger.info('Auto-backup scheduled', { schedule: backupSchedule });
   193→```
   194→
   195→### Pattern 4: SQLite Hot Backup via better-sqlite3
   196→
   197→**What:** `better-sqlite3`'s `.backup(destPath)` API performs an online backup (safe while the DB is open and being written to). It returns a Promise. Used in `exportDatabase()` in `index.electron.ts` — the same pattern applies in sync-server.
   198→
   199→**Source:** Confirmed in `packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.electron.ts` line 128: `await db.backup(name)`.
   200→
   201→The sync-server uses `WrappedDatabase` (db.ts) which wraps `better-sqlite3`. The underlying database is accessible; the backup function must open a raw `better-sqlite3` instance pointed at `account.sqlite`, call `.backup(destPath)`, then close it.
   202→
   203→**Example:**
   204→```typescript
   205→import Database from 'better-sqlite3';
   206→
   207→// Backup account.sqlite atomically
   208→const src = new Database(srcPath, { readonly: true });
   209→await src.backup(destPath);
   210→src.close();
   211→```
   212→
   213→### Pattern 5: Recovery Code Generation and Verification
   214→
   215→**What:** Generate 8 codes of format `XXXX-XXXX-XXXX` (12 alphanumeric chars in 3 groups of 4). Use `crypto.randomBytes(6).toString('hex').toUpperCase()` per code, split into groups. Hash each with bcrypt (cost 10 — lower than password's 12 since recovery codes are long random strings). Store as JSON array in `totp.recovery_codes`.
   216→
   217→On verification: iterate hashes, `bcrypt.compareSync(submitted, hash)`. On match, remove that hash from the array and save (mark consumed). Return `{ valid: true, remaining: N }`.
   218→
   219→### Anti-Patterns to Avoid
   220→
   221→- **Using `auth` table `extra_data` for structured TOTP data**: The column is a single text blob currently used for the bcrypt password hash. Overloading it requires JSON parsing everywhere and makes `extra_data` semantics ambiguous.
   222→- **Calling `loginWithPassword()` to check enrollment**: TOTP enrollment check must happen outside `loginWithPassword()` (which returns a token) — check after the call returns success.
   223→- **Synchronous file operations for backup**: Backup involves large file copies; use async Node.js fs promises (`fs.promises.copyFile`, etc.) or the async `db.backup()` to avoid blocking the event loop.
   224→- **Storing TOTP nonces in SQLite**: The intermediate nonces (5-min TTL) are ephemeral — an in-memory Map is correct (no persistence needed, no DB overhead).
   225→- **Using node-tar for archive creation**: Unnecessary dependency. Node.js built-in `tar` via pipe (`fs.createReadStream | zlib.createGzip | fs.createWriteStream`) handles the archive.
   226→- **Not scoping tar.gz to relative paths**: Archive budget directories with relative paths (not absolute) so the archive can be extracted anywhere. Use `path.relative(dataDir, filePath)` as entry name.

   229→
   230→## Don't Hand-Roll
   231→
   232→| Problem | Don't Build | Use Instead | Why |
   233→|---------|-------------|-------------|-----|
   234→| TOTP secret generation + verification | Custom HMAC-based OTP | `otpauth` | RFC 6238 compliance, time-window handling, QR URI generation |
   235→| QR code rendering | SVG/canvas from scratch | `qrcode` library | Correct QR error correction levels, supports both server-side data URI and client-side canvas rendering |
   236→| SQLite hot backup | File copy while DB open | `db.backup(destPath)` from better-sqlite3 | Atomic, WAL-aware, prevents corruption during concurrent writes |
   237→| TOTP QR URI format | Custom URI string | `otpauth.TOTP.toString()` | Generates correct `otpauth://` URI that authenticator apps parse |
   238→
   239→**Key insight:** The TOTP protocol has subtle edge cases (time window, replay prevention, base32 encoding) that `otpauth` handles correctly. The backup API has OS-level file locking concerns that `better-sqlite3`'s `.backup()` resolves. Do not implement either from scratch.

   242→
   243→## Common Pitfalls
   244→
   245→### Pitfall 1: TOTP Replay Attack Within Tolerance Window
   246→**What goes wrong:** The 1-step tolerance window allows codes valid 30 seconds before/after the current period. If the same code is accepted twice within this window, an attacker who intercepts the code can reuse it.
   247→**Why it happens:** Naive implementations only check if the code is valid, not if it was already used.
   248→**How to avoid:** Store `last_used_at` as the epoch timestamp of the TOTP period (floor to 30s boundary) in the `totp` table. Reject any code whose period timestamp equals `last_used_at`. Update `last_used_at` on successful verification.
   249→**Warning signs:** No `last_used_at` column in the TOTP schema.
   250→
   251→### Pitfall 2: Intermediate Nonce Leaking Password Correctness
   252→**What goes wrong:** If the server returns `{ needsTotp: true }` only after a valid password, an attacker can use the response to enumerate whether the password was correct.
   253→**Why it happens:** The two-step flow inherently leaks this.
   254→**How to avoid:** This is a known, accepted tradeoff for single-user apps (CONTEXT.md decision). For the implementation, ensure that failed TOTP attempts after a correct password still hit `trackAuthFailure()` and `writeAuditLog()` so the burst alerter fires on TOTP brute-force.
   255→**Warning signs:** TOTP failures not calling `trackAuthFailure(req.ip)`.
   256→
   257→### Pitfall 3: `auth` Table Method Collision
   258→**What goes wrong:** CONTEXT.md says store TOTP secret in `auth` table with `method='totp'`. The `auth` table currently has `extra_data TEXT` which stores a bcrypt hash for `method='password'`. Inserting a TOTP row with a JSON blob in `extra_data` works but the `needsBootstrap()` function checks `rows.length === 0` — a TOTP row would make the app think it's bootstrapped even with no password.
   259→**Why it happens:** `needsBootstrap()` does `SELECT * FROM auth` and returns `rows.length === 0`. Adding a `method='totp'` row would always return false.
   260→**How to avoid:** Use a separate `totp` table (not `auth` table). If the planner decides to follow the CONTEXT.md suggestion of `auth` table, `needsBootstrap()` must be updated to check `WHERE method = 'password' OR method = 'openid'`.
   261→**Warning signs:** `needsBootstrap()` returning false on a fresh install after TOTP migration runs.
   262→
   263→### Pitfall 4: Backup Running While SQLite is Being Written
   264→**What goes wrong:** If backup starts at 2 AM during an active sync (unlikely but possible), a naive file copy produces a corrupt backup.
   265→**Why it happens:** SQLite WAL mode allows concurrent readers but a raw `cp` skips WAL coordination.
   266→**How to avoid:** Always use `db.backup(destPath)` from better-sqlite3, which coordinates with the WAL and produces a consistent snapshot. Never use `fs.copyFile` directly on a live SQLite database.
   267→**Warning signs:** Using `fs.promises.copyFile` on `.sqlite` files instead of `db.backup()`.
   268→
   269→### Pitfall 5: Budget File Discovery
   270→**What goes wrong:** The backup needs to find all budget SQLite files under `/data`. The directory structure is `{ACTUAL_DATA_DIR}/{budget-uuid}/db.sqlite`. A hardcoded path will miss budgets or include unexpected files.
   271→**Why it happens:** Budget directories are UUID-named subdirectories; there's no registry of them outside the filesystem.
   272→**How to avoid:** Scan `ACTUAL_DATA_DIR` for subdirectories containing `db.sqlite`. Exclude the `backups/` directory itself from scanning to avoid recursive backup attempts.
   273→**Warning signs:** Hardcoded paths, not scanning for `db.sqlite` dynamically.
   274→
   275→### Pitfall 6: Recovery Codes Shown Once
   276→**What goes wrong:** If recovery codes are regenerated or re-shown after enrollment, users may assume the old codes are still valid.
   277→**Why it happens:** Poor state management of the enrollment flow.
   278→**How to avoid:** The server never returns plaintext recovery codes after the initial enrollment response. The `/totp/setup` endpoint returns codes once; subsequent `/totp/status` calls return only `{ enrolled: true, recoveryCodesRemaining: N }`. The client must make this clear with "Download / Copy now — these will not be shown again" UI.
   279→**Warning signs:** `/totp/status` returning plaintext codes.

   283→## Code Examples
   284→
   285→### TOTP Secret Generation and QR URI (otpauth 9.5.0)
   286→
   287→```typescript
   288→// Source: otpauth npm package docs (verified 2026-03-19)
   289→import { TOTP } from 'otpauth';
   290→
   291→// Generate a new TOTP secret for enrollment
   292→export function generateTotpSecret(issuer: string, accountName: string) {
   293→  const totp = new TOTP({
   294→    issuer,
   295→    label: accountName,
   296→    algorithm: 'SHA1',
   297→    digits: 6,
   298→    period: 30,
   299→  });
   300→  // totp.secret is the base32-encoded secret
   301→  // totp.toString() produces the otpauth:// URI for QR codes
   302→  return {
   303→    secret: totp.secret.base32,
   304→    uri: totp.toString(),
   305→  };
   306→}
   307→
   308→// Verify a TOTP code with 1-step window tolerance
   309→export function verifyTotpCode(
   310→  secret: string,
   311→  code: string,
   312→  lastUsedAt: number | null,
   313→): { valid: boolean; usedAt: number } {
   314→  const totp = new TOTP({ secret, algorithm: 'SHA1', digits: 6, period: 30 });
   315→  const delta = totp.validate({ token: code, window: 1 });
   316→  if (delta === null) return { valid: false, usedAt: lastUsedAt ?? 0 };
   317→
   318→  // The period timestamp for replay prevention
   319→  const periodTs = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000 / 30) + delta;
   320→  if (lastUsedAt !== null && periodTs === lastUsedAt) {
   321→    return { valid: false, usedAt: lastUsedAt }; // replay
   322→  }
   323→  return { valid: true, usedAt: periodTs };
   324→}
   325→```

   359→### SQLite Hot Backup via better-sqlite3
   360→
   361→```typescript
   362→// Source: better-sqlite3 docs + confirmed usage in index.electron.ts line 128
   363→import Database from 'better-sqlite3';
   364→import { promises as fsp } from 'node:fs';
   365→import path from 'node:path';
   366→
   367→export async function backupSqliteFile(srcPath: string, destPath: string): Promise<void> {
   368→  await fsp.mkdir(path.dirname(destPath), { recursive: true });
   369→  const db = new Database(srcPath, { readonly: true });
   370→  try {
   371→    await db.backup(destPath);
   372→  } finally {
   373→    db.close();
   374→  }
   375→}
   376→```

   432→## Open Questions
   433→
   434→1. **`auth` table vs separate `totp` table**
   435→   - What we know: CONTEXT.md says "Store TOTP secret encrypted in `auth` table with method='totp'". The `auth` table's structure supports this but `needsBootstrap()` queries the whole table.
   436→   - What's unclear: Whether the planner intends to modify `needsBootstrap()` or use a separate table.
   437→   - Recommendation: Use a separate `totp` table. Flag this to the planner — if `auth` table is chosen, `needsBootstrap()` must filter by `method IN ('password','openid')`.
   438→
   439→2. **TOTP secret encryption key source**
   440→   - What we know: Phase 5.2 uses `SECRET_KEY` env var for PBKDF2. The same infrastructure can derive a TOTP encryption key.
   441→   - What's unclear: Whether the planner wants a dedicated `TOTP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` env var or to reuse `SECRET_KEY` with a distinct salt.
   442→   - Recommendation: Reuse `SECRET_KEY` with a fixed domain-separation salt (`totp-secret-key`) to avoid requiring a new env var for existing deployments.
   443→
   444→3. **Budget file discovery scope**
   445→   - What we know: Budget files live at `{ACTUAL_DATA_DIR}/{uuid}/db.sqlite`. The `ACTUAL_DATA_DIR` env var is already used in the server.
   446→   - What's unclear: Whether the backup should also archive metadata.json files alongside db.sqlite per budget.
   447→   - Recommendation: Include `metadata.json` in the per-budget archive (needed for full restore). Reference `backups.ts` retention logic for prior art.
   448→
   449→4. **Manual "Backup Now" button**
   450→   - What we know: This is Claude's discretion per CONTEXT.md.
   451→   - Recommendation: Include it. A `POST /account/backup/trigger` endpoint (authenticated, admin only) is low-complexity and high-value for users who want an on-demand snapshot before risky operations.

# Phase 9: Feature Expansion - Context

**Gathered:** 2026-03-19
**Status:** Ready for planning

<domain>
## Phase Boundary

Implement two independent features: (1) optional 2FA/TOTP authentication for password-based login, and (2) automated server-side database backup with daily scheduling. Addresses audit findings fc-1 (2FA/TOTP) and fc-2 (backup automation).

</domain>

<decisions>
## Implementation Decisions

### TOTP Enrollment (fc-1)
- 2FA is optional, user-enabled via Settings page (single-user app, no mandatory enforcement needed)
- Enrollment flow: QR code + manual secret display in Settings, compatible with Google Authenticator/Authy/1Password
- Generate 8 one-time recovery codes at enrollment time (essential safety net if authenticator device is lost)
- Store TOTP secret encrypted in `auth` table with method='totp', recovery codes hashed in separate table or JSON field
- Use `otpauth` npm library (modern, ESM-native, zero-dependency, well-maintained)
- Audit log enrollment and disable events via existing Phase 7 audit system

### TOTP Verification (fc-1)
- Two-step login: password verification first, then TOTP challenge on a separate screen (doesn't leak password correctness to unenrolled users)
- TOTP required only for password login, not OpenID (OpenID providers handle their own MFA)
- 1-step time window tolerance (30 seconds before/after current period) to handle clock drift
- Track last used TOTP timestamp to prevent replay attacks within the tolerance window
- Recovery codes accepted as TOTP alternative, each code single-use, mark as consumed after use
- Failed TOTP attempts logged to audit log, count toward existing auth failure burst alert (Phase 7)

### Backup Automation (fc-2)
- Server-side cron job in scheduler.ts (extends existing node-cron pattern, runs without browser open)
- Daily backup at 2 AM via node-cron (5-field format: `0 2 * * *`)
- Back up full /data directory: account.sqlite + all budget SQLite files
- Use SQLite `.backup()` API for atomic database copy (prevents corruption from concurrent access)
- Archive budget directories into tar.gz for space efficiency
- Store backups in /data/backups/ within Docker volume (persists across restarts, no cloud dependency)

### Backup Retention (fc-2)
- Keep last 7 daily backups (one week of snapshots, sufficient for personal use)
- Automatic cleanup of backups older than 7 days after each successful backup run
- Backup failure triggers alert via existing Phase 7 webhook alerter (new event_type: 'backup_failure')
- Show last backup time and status on Settings page (matches sync status visibility pattern)

### Claude's Discretion
- TOTP QR code rendering approach (inline SVG, canvas, or library like `qrcode`)
- Exact recovery code format (alphanumeric groups, length)
- TOTP secret encryption key derivation (reuse existing PBKDF2 infrastructure or separate)
- Backup archive naming convention and directory structure within /data/backups/
- Whether to add a manual "Backup Now" button alongside the automated schedule
- Settings page layout for 2FA and backup sections

</decisions>

- `auth` table: Stores auth methods with `method`, `display_name`, `extra_data`, `active` columns. TOTP secret can follow same pattern (method='totp').

- Audit events follow `{ event_type, actor, ip_address, outcome, details }` schema
- Alert events follow `{ event_type, message, timestamp, severity }` schema

- `app-account.ts /login`: After password verification succeeds, check if TOTP is enrolled; if yes, return intermediate state requiring TOTP code

- Desktop client Settings page: New sections for 2FA management and backup status display

# Phase 9: Feature Expansion - Context

**Gathered:** 2026-03-19
**Status:** Ready for planning

<domain>
## Phase Boundary

Implement two independent features: (1) optional 2FA/TOTP authentication for password-based login, and (2) automated server-side database backup with daily scheduling. Addresses audit findings fc-1 (2FA/TOTP) and fc-2 (backup automation).

</domain>

<decisions>
## Implementation Decisions

### TOTP Enrollment (fc-1)
- 2FA is optional, user-enabled via Settings page (single-user app, no mandatory enforcement needed)
- Enrollment flow: QR code + manual secret display in Settings, compatible with Google Authenticator/Authy/1Password
- Generate 8 one-time recovery codes at enrollment time (essential safety net if authenticator device is lost)
- Store TOTP secret in a separate `totp` table (not `auth` table) to avoid `needsBootstrap()` collision; secret AES-256-GCM encrypted, recovery codes bcrypt-hashed in JSON field
- Use `otpauth` npm library (modern, ESM-native, zero-dependency, well-maintained)
- Audit log enrollment and disable events via existing Phase 7 audit system

### TOTP Verification (fc-1)
- Two-step login: password verification first, then TOTP challenge on a separate screen (doesn't leak password correctness to unenrolled users)
- TOTP required only for password login, not OpenID (OpenID providers handle their own MFA)
- 1-step time window tolerance (30 seconds before/after current period) to handle clock drift
- Track last used TOTP timestamp to prevent replay attacks within the tolerance window
- Recovery codes accepted as TOTP alternative, each code single-use, mark as consumed after use
- Failed TOTP attempts logged to audit log, count toward existing auth failure burst alert (Phase 7)

### Backup Automation (fc-2)
- Server-side cron job in scheduler.ts (extends existing node-cron pattern, runs without browser open)
- Daily backup at 2 AM via node-cron (5-field format: `0 2 * * *`)
- Back up full /data directory: account.sqlite + all budget SQLite files
- Use SQLite `.backup()` API for atomic database copy (prevents corruption from concurrent access)
- Archive budget directories into tar.gz for space efficiency
- Store backups in /data/backups/ within Docker volume (persists across restarts, no cloud dependency)

### Backup Retention (fc-2)
- Keep last 7 daily backups (one week of snapshots, sufficient for personal use)
- Automatic cleanup of backups older than 7 days after each successful backup run
- Backup failure triggers alert via existing Phase 7 webhook alerter (new event_type: 'backup_failure')

    14→## Implementation Decisions
    15→
    16→### TOTP Enrollment (fc-1)
    17→- 2FA is optional, user-enabled via Settings page (single-user app, no mandatory enforcement needed)
    18→- Enrollment flow: QR code + manual secret display in Settings, compatible with Google Authenticator/Authy/1Password
    19→- Generate 8 one-time recovery codes at enrollment time (essential safety net if authenticator device is lost)
    20→- Store TOTP secret in a separate `totp` table (not `auth` table) to avoid `needsBootstrap()` collision; secret AES-256-GCM encrypted, recovery codes bcrypt-hashed in JSON field
    21→- Use `otpauth` npm library (modern, ESM-native, zero-dependency, well-maintained)
    22→- Audit log enrollment and disable events via existing Phase 7 audit system
    23→
    24→### TOTP Verification (fc-1)
    25→- Two-step login: password verification first, then TOTP challenge on a separate screen (doesn't leak password correctness to unenrolled users)
    26→- TOTP required only for password login, not OpenID (OpenID providers handle their own MFA)
    27→- 1-step time window tolerance (30 seconds before/after current period) to handle clock drift
    28→- Track last used TOTP timestamp to prevent replay attacks within the tolerance window
    29→- Recovery codes accepted as TOTP alternative, each code single-use, mark as consumed after use
    30→- Failed TOTP attempts logged to audit log, count toward existing auth failure burst alert (Phase 7)
    31→
    32→### Backup Automation (fc-2)
    33→- Server-side cron job in scheduler.ts (extends existing node-cron pattern, runs without browser open)
    34→- Daily backup at 2 AM via node-cron (5-field format: `0 2 * * *`)
    35→- Back up full /data directory: account.sqlite + all budget SQLite files
    36→- Use SQLite `.backup()` API for atomic database copy (prevents corruption from concurrent access)
    37→- Archive budget directories into tar.gz for space efficiency
    38→- Store backups in /data/backups/ within Docker volume (persists across restarts, no cloud dependency)
    39→
    40→### Backup Retention (fc-2)
    41→- Keep last 7 daily backups (one week of snapshots, sufficient for personal use)
    42→- Automatic cleanup of backups older than 7 days after each successful backup run
    43→- Backup failure triggers alert via existing Phase 7 webhook alerter (new event_type: 'backup_failure')
    44→- Show last backup time and status on Settings page (matches sync status visibility pattern)
    45→
    46→### Claude's Discretion
    47→- TOTP QR code rendering approach (inline SVG, canvas, or library like `qrcode`)
    48→- Exact recovery code format (alphanumeric groups, length)
    49→- TOTP secret encryption key derivation (reuse existing PBKDF2 infrastructure or separate)
    50→- Backup archive naming convention and directory structure within /data/backups/
    51→- Whether to add a manual "Backup Now" button alongside the automated schedule
    52→- Settings page layout for 2FA and backup sections

   136→
   137→### Pattern 1: Intermediate TOTP Challenge State
   138→
   139→The login endpoint cannot return a session token when TOTP is enrolled; it must return a short-lived nonce the client uses to complete the TOTP challenge.
   140→
   141→**What:** After `loginWithPassword()` succeeds, check if TOTP is enrolled. If yes, generate a short-lived nonce (UUID, expires in 5 minutes, stored in-memory Map), return `{ needsTotp: true, totpNonce: <nonce> }` instead of `{ token }`. Client calls `/totp/challenge` with `{ totpNonce, code }` to redeem the nonce for a real session token.
   142→
   143→**When to use:** Only on the `default` (password) branch of the `/login` switch in `app-account.ts`. OpenID and header branches are unaffected.
   144→
   145→**Example (server-side login modification):**
   146→```typescript
   147→// In app-account.ts /login — after tokenRes = loginWithPassword(password)
   148→if (!tokenRes.error && isTotpEnrolled()) {
   149→  const nonce = uuidv4();
   150→  totpNonces.set(nonce, { expiresAt: Date.now() + 5 * 60 * 1000 });
   151→  res.send({ status: 'ok', data: { needsTotp: true, totpNonce: nonce } });
   152→  return;
   153→}
   154→```
   155→
   156→### Pattern 2: TOTP Secret Storage (Encrypted)
   157→
   158→**What:** Store TOTP secret AES-256-GCM encrypted. Key derived from `process.env.SECRET_KEY` (already used in Phase 5.2) + a fixed salt using PBKDF2 (100K iterations, same as existing password key derivation pattern). Store `{ iv, authTag, ciphertext }` as JSON in a new `totp` table.
   159→
   160→**Schema (added to `runAuditMigrations()` pattern — new idempotent migration helper):**
   161→```sql
   162→CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS totp (
   163→  id           INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
   164→  user_id      TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
   165→  secret_enc   TEXT    NOT NULL,  -- JSON: { iv, authTag, ciphertext } base64-encoded
   166→  enrolled_at  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%s','now')),
   167→  last_used_at INTEGER,           -- epoch seconds, for replay prevention
   168→  recovery_codes TEXT NOT NULL    -- JSON array of bcrypt hashes
   169→);
   170→```
   171→
   172→Note: CONTEXT.md says "Store TOTP secret encrypted in `auth` table with method='totp'". However, the `auth` table's `extra_data` column stores only a single text blob (currently the bcrypt password hash). Storing a structured JSON blob in `extra_data` would work functionally but mixes concerns. The clean approach — and what the planner should verify — is a separate `totp` table. Both approaches are viable; the planner should pick one consistently. **Recommendation: separate `totp` table for clarity and replay-prevention (`last_used_at` column).**
   173→
   174→### Pattern 3: Backup Cron Extension
   175→
   176→**What:** Add a second `cron.schedule()` call in `startScheduler()`, guarded by `ENABLE_AUTO_BACKUP !== 'false'` (opt-out, enabled by default — matches the decision that backup is a safety feature).
   177→
   178→**Example:**
   179→```typescript
   180→// scheduler.ts — inside startScheduler(), after existing sync cron
   181→const backupSchedule = process.env.BACKUP_CRON_SCHEDULE ?? '0 2 * * *';
   182→cron.schedule(backupSchedule, () => {
   183→  runBackup().catch(err => {
   184→    logger.error('Backup failed', { error: err.message });
   185→    triggerAlert({
   186→      event_type: 'backup_failure',
   187→      message: `Daily backup failed: ${err.message}`,
   188→      severity: 'error',
   189→    }).catch(() => {});
   190→  });
   191→});
   192→logger.info('Auto-backup scheduled', { schedule: backupSchedule });
   193→```
   194→
   195→### Pattern 4: SQLite Hot Backup via better-sqlite3
   196→
   197→**What:** `better-sqlite3`'s `.backup(destPath)` API performs an online backup (safe while the DB is open and being written to). It returns a Promise. Used in `exportDatabase()` in `index.electron.ts` — the same pattern applies in sync-server.
   198→
   199→**Source:** Confirmed in `packages/loot-core/src/platform/server/sqlite/index.electron.ts` line 128: `await db.backup(name)`.
   200→
   201→The sync-server uses `WrappedDatabase` (db.ts) which wraps `better-sqlite3`. The underlying database is accessible; the backup function must open a raw `better-sqlite3` instance pointed at `account.sqlite`, call `.backup(destPath)`, then close it.
   202→
   203→**Example:**
   204→```typescript
   205→import Database from 'better-sqlite3';
   206→
   207→// Backup account.sqlite atomically
   208→const src = new Database(srcPath, { readonly: true });
   209→await src.backup(destPath);
   210→src.close();
   211→```
   212→
   213→### Pattern 5: Recovery Code Generation and Verification
   214→
   215→**What:** Generate 8 codes of format `XXXX-XXXX-XXXX` (12 alphanumeric chars in 3 groups of 4). Use `crypto.randomBytes(6).toString('hex').toUpperCase()` per code, split into groups. Hash each with bcrypt (cost 10 — lower than password's 12 since recovery codes are long random strings). Store as JSON array in `totp.recovery_codes`.
   216→
   217→On verification: iterate hashes, `bcrypt.compareSync(submitted, hash)`. On match, remove that hash from the array and save (mark consumed). Return `{ valid: true, remaining: N }`.
   218→
   219→### Anti-Patterns to Avoid
   220→
   221→- **Using `auth` table `extra_data` for structured TOTP data**: The column is a single text blob currently used for the bcrypt password hash. Overloading it requires JSON parsing everywhere and makes `extra_data` semantics ambiguous.
   222→- **Calling `loginWithPassword()` to check enrollment**: TOTP enrollment check must happen outside `loginWithPassword()` (which returns a token) — check after the call returns success.
   223→- **Synchronous file operations for backup**: Backup involves large file copies; use async Node.js fs promises (`fs.promises.copyFile`, etc.) or the async `db.backup()` to avoid blocking the event loop.
   224→- **Storing TOTP nonces in SQLite**: The intermediate nonces (5-min TTL) are ephemeral — an in-memory Map is correct (no persistence needed, no DB overhead).
   225→- **Using node-tar for archive creation**: Unnecessary dependency. Node.js built-in `tar` via pipe (`fs.createReadStream | zlib.createGzip | fs.createWriteStream`) handles the archive.
   226→- **Not scoping tar.gz to relative paths**: Archive budget directories with relative paths (not absolute) so the archive can be extracted anywhere. Use `path.relative(dataDir, filePath)` as entry name.

   229→
   230→## Don't Hand-Roll
   231→
   232→| Problem | Don't Build | Use Instead | Why |
   233→|---------|-------------|-------------|-----|
   234→| TOTP secret generation + verification | Custom HMAC-based OTP | `otpauth` | RFC 6238 compliance, time-window handling, QR URI generation |
   235→| QR code rendering | SVG/canvas from scratch | `qrcode` library | Correct QR error correction levels, supports both server-side data URI and client-side canvas rendering |
   236→| SQLite hot backup | File copy while DB open | `db.backup(destPath)` from better-sqlite3 | Atomic, WAL-aware, prevents corruption during concurrent writes |
   237→| TOTP QR URI format | Custom URI string | `otpauth.TOTP.toString()` | Generates correct `otpauth://` URI that authenticator apps parse |
   238→
   239→**Key insight:** The TOTP protocol has subtle edge cases (time window, replay prevention, base32 encoding) that `otpauth` handles correctly. The backup API has OS-level file locking concerns that `better-sqlite3`'s `.backup()` resolves. Do not implement either from scratch.

   242→
   243→## Common Pitfalls
   244→
   245→### Pitfall 1: TOTP Replay Attack Within Tolerance Window
   246→**What goes wrong:** The 1-step tolerance window allows codes valid 30 seconds before/after the current period. If the same code is accepted twice within this window, an attacker who intercepts the code can reuse it.
   247→**Why it happens:** Naive implementations only check if the code is valid, not if it was already used.
   248→**How to avoid:** Store `last_used_at` as the epoch timestamp of the TOTP period (floor to 30s boundary) in the `totp` table. Reject any code whose period timestamp equals `last_used_at`. Update `last_used_at` on successful verification.
   249→**Warning signs:** No `last_used_at` column in the TOTP schema.
   250→
   251→### Pitfall 2: Intermediate Nonce Leaking Password Correctness
   252→**What goes wrong:** If the server returns `{ needsTotp: true }` only after a valid password, an attacker can use the response to enumerate whether the password was correct.
   253→**Why it happens:** The two-step flow inherently leaks this.
   254→**How to avoid:** This is a known, accepted tradeoff for single-user apps (CONTEXT.md decision). For the implementation, ensure that failed TOTP attempts after a correct password still hit `trackAuthFailure()` and `writeAuditLog()` so the burst alerter fires on TOTP brute-force.
   255→**Warning signs:** TOTP failures not calling `trackAuthFailure(req.ip)`.
   256→
   257→### Pitfall 3: `auth` Table Method Collision
   258→**What goes wrong:** CONTEXT.md says store TOTP secret in `auth` table with `method='totp'`. The `auth` table currently has `extra_data TEXT` which stores a bcrypt hash for `method='password'`. Inserting a TOTP row with a JSON blob in `extra_data` works but the `needsBootstrap()` function checks `rows.length === 0` — a TOTP row would make the app think it's bootstrapped even with no password.
   259→**Why it happens:** `needsBootstrap()` does `SELECT * FROM auth` and returns `rows.length === 0`. Adding a `method='totp'` row would always return false.
   260→**How to avoid:** Use a separate `totp` table (not `auth` table). If the planner decides to follow the CONTEXT.md suggestion of `auth` table, `needsBootstrap()` must be updated to check `WHERE method = 'password' OR method = 'openid'`.
   261→**Warning signs:** `needsBootstrap()` returning false on a fresh install after TOTP migration runs.
   262→
   263→### Pitfall 4: Backup Running While SQLite is Being Written
   264→**What goes wrong:** If backup starts at 2 AM during an active sync (unlikely but possible), a naive file copy produces a corrupt backup.
   265→**Why it happens:** SQLite WAL mode allows concurrent readers but a raw `cp` skips WAL coordination.
   266→**How to avoid:** Always use `db.backup(destPath)` from better-sqlite3, which coordinates with the WAL and produces a consistent snapshot. Never use `fs.copyFile` directly on a live SQLite database.
   267→**Warning signs:** Using `fs.promises.copyFile` on `.sqlite` files instead of `db.backup()`.
   268→
   269→### Pitfall 5: Budget File Discovery
   270→**What goes wrong:** The backup needs to find all budget SQLite files under `/data`. The directory structure is `{ACTUAL_DATA_DIR}/{budget-uuid}/db.sqlite`. A hardcoded path will miss budgets or include unexpected files.
   271→**Why it happens:** Budget directories are UUID-named subdirectories; there's no registry of them outside the filesystem.
   272→**How to avoid:** Scan `ACTUAL_DATA_DIR` for subdirectories containing `db.sqlite`. Exclude the `backups/` directory itself from scanning to avoid recursive backup attempts.
   273→**Warning signs:** Hardcoded paths, not scanning for `db.sqlite` dynamically.
   274→
   275→### Pitfall 6: Recovery Codes Shown Once
   276→**What goes wrong:** If recovery codes are regenerated or re-shown after enrollment, users may assume the old codes are still valid.
   277→**Why it happens:** Poor state management of the enrollment flow.
   278→**How to avoid:** The server never returns plaintext recovery codes after the initial enrollment response. The `/totp/setup` endpoint returns codes once; subsequent `/totp/status` calls return only `{ enrolled: true, recoveryCodesRemaining: N }`. The client must make this clear with "Download / Copy now — these will not be shown again" UI.
   279→**Warning signs:** `/totp/status` returning plaintext codes.

   283→## Code Examples
   284→
   285→### TOTP Secret Generation and QR URI (otpauth 9.5.0)
   286→
   287→```typescript
   288→// Source: otpauth npm package docs (verified 2026-03-19)
   289→import { TOTP } from 'otpauth';
   290→
   291→// Generate a new TOTP secret for enrollment
   292→export function generateTotpSecret(issuer: string, accountName: string) {
   293→  const totp = new TOTP({
   294→    issuer,
   295→    label: accountName,
   296→    algorithm: 'SHA1',
   297→    digits: 6,
   298→    period: 30,
   299→  });
   300→  // totp.secret is the base32-encoded secret
   301→  // totp.toString() produces the otpauth:// URI for QR codes
   302→  return {
   303→    secret: totp.secret.base32,
   304→    uri: totp.toString(),
   305→  };
   306→}
   307→
   308→// Verify a TOTP code with 1-step window tolerance
   309→export function verifyTotpCode(
   310→  secret: string,
   311→  code: string,
   312→  lastUsedAt: number | null,
   313→): { valid: boolean; usedAt: number } {
   314→  const totp = new TOTP({ secret, algorithm: 'SHA1', digits: 6, period: 30 });
   315→  const delta = totp.validate({ token: code, window: 1 });
   316→  if (delta === null) return { valid: false, usedAt: lastUsedAt ?? 0 };
   317→
   318→  // The period timestamp for replay prevention
   319→  const periodTs = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000 / 30) + delta;
   320→  if (lastUsedAt !== null && periodTs === lastUsedAt) {
   321→    return { valid: false, usedAt: lastUsedAt }; // replay
   322→  }
   323→  return { valid: true, usedAt: periodTs };
   324→}
   325→```

   359→### SQLite Hot Backup via better-sqlite3
   360→
   361→```typescript
   362→// Source: better-sqlite3 docs + confirmed usage in index.electron.ts line 128
   363→import Database from 'better-sqlite3';
   364→import { promises as fsp } from 'node:fs';
   365→import path from 'node:path';
   366→
   367→export async function backupSqliteFile(srcPath: string, destPath: string): Promise<void> {
   368→  await fsp.mkdir(path.dirname(destPath), { recursive: true });
   369→  const db = new Database(srcPath, { readonly: true });
   370→  try {
   371→    await db.backup(destPath);
   372→  } finally {
   373→    db.close();
   374→  }
   375→}

   181→    **createTarGz(sourceDir: string, outputPath: string): Promise<void>**
   182→    Helper function to archive a directory into a .tar.gz file using Node.js built-in modules (no `node-tar` dependency).
   183→
   184→    Implementation approach: Create a simple tar archive using raw binary writes. The tar format is straightforward for this use case (a flat set of files within subdirectories).
   185→
   186→    Alternative simpler approach: Since the backup directory contains only SQLite files and metadata.json, use a simpler strategy:
   187→    - Walk the backup directory to collect all files with their relative paths
   188→    - For each file, write a tar header (512-byte block: name, size, type, checksum) followed by file content padded to 512-byte boundary
   189→    - Pipe the resulting tar stream through `createGzip()` to produce `.tar.gz`
   190→
   191→    ```typescript
   192→    async function createTarGz(sourceDir: string, outputPath: string): Promise<void> {
   193→      const files: Array<{ relativePath: string; absolutePath: string; size: number }> = [];
   194→      // Recursively collect all files
   195→      async function collectFiles(dir: string, prefix: string) {
   196→        const entries = await fsp.readdir(dir, { withFileTypes: true });
   197→        for (const entry of entries) {
   198→          const absPath = path.join(dir, entry.name);
   199→          const relPath = prefix ? `${prefix}/${entry.name}` : entry.name;
   200→          if (entry.isDirectory()) {
   201→            await collectFiles(absPath, relPath);
   202→          } else if (entry.isFile()) {
   203→            const stat = await fsp.stat(absPath);
   204→            files.push({ relativePath: relPath, absolutePath: absPath, size: stat.size });
   205→          }
   206→        }
   207→      }
   208→      await collectFiles(sourceDir, '');
   209→
   210→      // Write tar.gz: tar header per file + content + padding, then gzip
   211→      const { Readable } = await import('node:stream');
   212→      const tarStream = new Readable({ read() {} });
   213→
   214→      for (const file of files) {
   215→        // Create 512-byte tar header
   216→        const header = Buffer.alloc(512);
   217→        // Name (100 bytes)
   218→        header.write(file.relativePath.slice(0, 100), 0, 100, 'utf8');
   219→        // Mode (8 bytes at offset 100)
   220→        header.write('0000644\0', 100, 8, 'utf8');
   221→        // UID/GID (8 bytes each at 108, 116)
   222→        header.write('0001000\0', 108, 8, 'utf8');
   223→        header.write('0001000\0', 116, 8, 'utf8');
   224→        // Size (12 bytes at offset 124, octal)
   225→        header.write(file.size.toString(8).padStart(11, '0') + '\0', 124, 12, 'utf8');
   226→        // Mtime (12 bytes at 136)
   227→        header.write(Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000).toString(8).padStart(11, '0') + '\0', 136, 12, 'utf8');
   228→        // Type flag (1 byte at 156): '0' = regular file
   229→        header.write('0', 156, 1, 'utf8');
   230→        // Checksum placeholder (8 bytes at 148): spaces initially
   231→        header.write('        ', 148, 8, 'utf8');
   232→        // Compute checksum (sum of all bytes treating checksum field as spaces)
   233→        let checksum = 0;
   234→        for (let i = 0; i < 512; i++) checksum += header[i];
   235→        header.write(checksum.toString(8).padStart(6, '0') + '\0 ', 148, 8, 'utf8');
   236→
   237→        tarStream.push(header);
   238→        // File content
   239→        const content = await fsp.readFile(file.absolutePath);
   240→        tarStream.push(content);
   241→        // Pad to 512-byte boundary
   242→        const remainder = content.length % 512;
   243→        if (remainder > 0) tarStream.push(Buffer.alloc(512 - remainder));
   244→      }
   245→      // End-of-archive marker (two 512-byte zero blocks)
   246→      tarStream.push(Buffer.alloc(1024));
   247→      tarStream.push(null); // end stream
   248→
   249→      const gzip = createGzip();
   250→      const output = createWriteStream(outputPath);
   251→      await pipeline(tarStream, gzip, output);
   252→    }
   253→    ```

     8→
     9→Implement two independent features: (1) optional 2FA/TOTP authentication for password-based login, and (2) automated server-side database backup with daily scheduling. Addresses audit findings fc-1 (2FA/TOTP) and fc-2 (backup automation).

    13→<decisions>
    14→## Implementation Decisions
    15→
    16→### TOTP Enrollment (fc-1)
    17→- 2FA is optional, user-enabled via Settings page (single-user app, no mandatory enforcement needed)
    18→- Enrollment flow: QR code + manual secret display in Settings, compatible with Google Authenticator/Authy/1Password
    19→- Generate 8 one-time recovery codes at enrollment time (essential safety net if authenticator device is lost)
    20→- Store TOTP secret in a separate `totp` table (not `auth` table) to avoid `needsBootstrap()` collision; secret AES-256-GCM encrypted, recovery codes bcrypt-hashed in JSON field
    21→- Use `otpauth` npm library (modern, ESM-native, zero-dependency, well-maintained)
    22→- Audit log enrollment and disable events via existing Phase 7 audit system
    23→
    24→### TOTP Verification (fc-1)
    25→- Two-step login: password verification first, then TOTP challenge on a separate screen (doesn't leak password correctness to unenrolled users)
    26→- TOTP required only for password login, not OpenID (OpenID providers handle their own MFA)
    27→- 1-step time window tolerance (30 seconds before/after current period) to handle clock drift
    28→- Track last used TOTP timestamp to prevent replay attacks within the tolerance window
    29→- Recovery codes accepted as TOTP alternative, each code single-use, mark as consumed after use
    30→- Failed TOTP attempts logged to audit log, count toward existing auth failure burst alert (Phase 7)
    31→
    32→### Backup Automation (fc-2)
    33→- Server-side cron job in scheduler.ts (extends existing node-cron pattern, runs without browser open)
    34→- Daily backup at 2 AM via node-cron (5-field format: `0 2 * * *`)
    35→- Back up full /data directory: account.sqlite + all budget SQLite files
    36→- Use SQLite `.backup()` API for atomic database copy (prevents corruption from concurrent access)
    37→- Archive budget directories into tar.gz for space efficiency
    38→- Store backups in /data/backups/ within Docker volume (persists across restarts, no cloud dependency)
    39→
    40→### Backup Retention (fc-2)
    41→- Keep last 7 daily backups (one week of snapshots, sufficient for personal use)
    42→- Automatic cleanup of backups older than 7 days after each successful backup run
    43→- Backup failure triggers alert via existing Phase 7 webhook alerter (new event_type: 'backup_failure')
    44→- Show last backup time and status on Settings page (matches sync status visibility pattern)
    45→

    47→- TOTP QR code rendering approach (inline SVG, canvas, or library like `qrcode`)
    48→- Exact recovery code format (alphanumeric groups, length)
    49→- TOTP secret encryption key derivation (reuse existing PBKDF2 infrastructure or separate)
    50→- Backup archive naming convention and directory structure within /data/backups/
    51→- Whether to add a manual "Backup Now" button alongside the automated schedule

1→# Phase 9: Feature Expansion - Research
     2→
     3→**Researched:** 2026-03-19
     4→**Domain:** TOTP/2FA authentication + server-side SQLite backup automation
     5→**Confidence:** HIGH
     6→
     7→## Summary
     8→
     9→Phase 9 implements two independent server-side features: optional TOTP-based 2FA for password login, and automated daily backup of the /data directory. Both features integrate with established Phase 7 infrastructure (audit logging, alerter, metrics) and the existing node-cron scheduler pattern in scheduler.ts.
    10→
    11→The TOTP feature requires one new npm dependency (`otpauth` 9.5.0) and a QR code renderer on the desktop client (the `qrcode` library is the standard choice, version 1.5.4). The backup feature requires no new dependencies — better-sqlite3 (already present at ^12.6.2) provides the `.backup()` API, and Node.js built-in `node:fs`, `node:path`, and `node:zlib` handle archive creation without needing `node-tar`. The `fs.createReadStream`/`zlib.createGzip`/`fs.createWriteStream` pipeline is idiomatic Node.js for tar.gz creation.
    12→
    13→The TOTP enrollment and verification flow intercepts the existing `loginWithPassword()` path in `password.ts`. After a successful password check, the server returns an intermediate state (`{ needsTotp: true, totpToken: <short-lived-nonce> }`) instead of a session token. The client presents a TOTP challenge screen, submits the code to a new `/totp/verify` endpoint, and receives the real session token on success. All TOTP metadata is stored in a new `totp` table keyed to the user, separate from the `auth` table which stores the password hash.
    14→
    15→**Primary recommendation:** Implement TOTP using `otpauth` for secret generation and verification. Use `qrcode` for QR rendering on the client. Extend `scheduler.ts` with a second `cron.schedule()` call for backup. Store TOTP secrets AES-256-GCM encrypted using a server-derived key (PBKDF2 from server secret). Archive backups with Node.js built-in streams.
